# ADR-049: The external floor replaces apps/floor, one family of lines at a time

The Floor was rewritten as a standalone engine, [re-cinq/floor](https://github.com/re-cinq/floor), and runs in the same cluster as Lore. This ADR records how Lore moves onto it: through `@re-cinq/floor-client` only, one family of assembly lines per slice, with both floors running side by side until the last line has moved and `apps/floor` is deleted.

## User story

As the team running Lore, we want every assembly line to run on the external floor ([re-cinq/floor](https://github.com/re-cinq/floor)) or not exist at all, so that `apps/floor` can be deleted and Lore runs on one engine.

# Feature Specification: Station Consolidation

## Functional Requirements

> **2026-10-02.** This describes Lore's own Floor (`apps/floor`), which was deleted (`specs/external-floor` FR16.10); it is kept as the record of what the old engine did.

## What this deletes

- `apps/floor`: about 17,500 lines and 113 test files. The old walk of assembly lines, the worker and watcher of single-agent tasks, its event registry, its HTTP server, the dark-factory auto-merge evaluation.
- Its Helm subchart (`floor-helm`), its build workflow, and its entries in the workspace, the lockfile, the layering file, the lint configuration and the PR checks.
- The five ticks only it answered (`stale_task_check`, `assembly_line_reaper`, `agent_watcher_reconcile`, `lease_reaper`, `llm_credit_probe`).
- Its bus subscription: migration 0095 removes the `floor` subscriber and the deliveries nobody would claim. Without it every event would keep one pending delivery forever.

## What changes outside it

- `POST /api/task-turns/{taskId}` stores a local run's tra…

# Feature Specification: Assembly Line Run Visualization

## Background: retired with Lore's own Floor (2026-10-02)

These statements described behaviour of `apps/floor`, the assembly-line engine Lore ran itself. It was deleted on 2026-10-02 (epic #2342, ADR-049): the external floor runs every line now, so the tests that validated these went with the code. They are kept as the record of what the old engine did.
